item.title: Hedgerow completely obstructing vision when turning right onto ermin street from Abbotswood Road. Oncoming traffic cannot be seen safely until you are in the roundabout. It is also covering street signs., 4th November
item.description:
The hedgerow to the right-hand side as you approach the mini roundabout from Abbotswood Road onto Ermin Street has grown outward to the point that you can no longer see what traffic is coming down the hill from the Shell Garage, until you are within the roundabout. You can see from the photo where the hedge should finish inline with the street sign that has been covered. It's making it dangerous and difficult to pull out, particularly in heavy traffic.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 103, Ermin Street, Gloucester

item.title: Urgent Street Light Repair Required – Gloucester Road, Cheltenham, 3rd November
item.description:
Hello, I'm writing to report a street light that has stopped working on Gloucester Road, Cheltenham. The street light is located to the right of number 228 Gloucester Road (if you're facing the property), opposite St Mark's Methodist Church. The lack of lighting is creating significant darkness outside my property and along this section of the road, raising concerns about pedestrian safety and security, particularly during the darker evenings. I would be grateful if this could be investigated and repaired as a matter of urgency. Could you please confirm when the light is likely to be repaired? Many thanks.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 232, Gloucester Road, Kingsditch, Cheltenham, Cheltenham

item.title: The landowner'i sign giving 'permitted access' to the bridleway (and footpath)., 3rd November
item.description:
Concerned a farm track that is designated KSE17. Where it enters Sevenhampton, there is a new gate (replacing an older one) alongside the first habitation on which has been mounted a green waymark style sign suggesting that the landowner is giving 'permitted access' to the bridleway (and footpath). The new landowner living in the cottage alongside the new gate appears to own land on both sides of KSE17. I was not aware that a PROW could be downgraded in this way.
